title: [decision] A non-object metadata name shared by two installed packages often resolves to one package silently: which naming contract replaces ADR-0048 §3.4?
body:
epic:#3600#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPXwX1YfHyKJUh4agu

Filing-gate category: ② decision the maintainer directed. Maintainer, verbatim (Claude Code session, 2026-11-06), on the seat's bare-name audit: 「裸名的问题立决策卡」. Origin: the scenario-library epic objectstack-ai/cloud#3600 (gallery apps installed side by side in one environment).

## Maintainer brief

- **The problem in one sentence:** when two installed apps each ship, say, an automation or a button with the same name, the platform often runs only one of them — usually silently, and which one depends on install order.
- **What you decide:** how a non-object metadata name stays unambiguous across installed packages. Options A, B-lite, B, C, D below; the seat recommends **C, phased**.
- **If nothing is decided:** every new marketplace or gallery app that reuses a common name (`send_email`, `approve`, `sales_rep`) can silently disable part of another app; nobody sees an error.

## Background

Only object names must carry the package namespace (`<ns>_<short>`, ADR-0129). Every other metadata type — flows, actions, hooks, picklists, pages, dashboards, reports, apps, datasets, api items, email templates, agents, tools, skills, jobs, connectors, webhooks, … — has a bare name. ADR-0048 decided that two packages MAY ship the same bare name: storage keeps both (unique on type, name, package_id, bundle_member), §3.3 says "each caller resolves to its own package's item", and §3.4 says two distinct packages "coexist on the same bare name by construction". The 2026-10-08 narrowing of §3.4 states its premise, "§3.4 rests on every caller carrying its package id", and took the security catalog out because assignments carry no package context. For `action` the ADR never claimed package scoping (§6 lists it as intentionally global; same-name actions on different objects are keyed `objectName:name` and do not collide).

## Governing text

- **ADR-0048** (`docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md`): §3.3 (lines 217-256) package-scoped resolution, and a context-free read "is best-effort: it returns the first match and the caller is expected to pass the package id when it cares"; §3.4 (261-266) coexistence "by construction", narrowed 2026-10-08 for positions, permission sets and capabilities (#22197 / #22307); §5's "[done] lint warns on non-prefixed app/page/dashboard/flow/action/report/dataset" (333-335) is out of date (below). Superseded in part by ADR-0146 D2/D8 for a base's dependency closure only.
- **`os lint` `naming/namespace-prefix`** (`packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts:319-326`): today flags intra-package duplicates only, and its message says "Distinct packages may reuse the same name freely; the namespace prefix is an optional convention, not a collision-avoidance requirement".
- **ADR-0129** (Accepted): the literal object prefix gives the AI author "exactly one writing style".
- **ADR-0028** (Deferred): package-scoped identity with qualified cross references; the seat's ruling record on objectstack-ai/cloud#3600 (comment 6676044775) records that this direction makes AI authors err more.
- **Security catalog rule** (ruling Q4 = A on #15196; the ADR-0048 2026-10-08 addendum).
- **Unmanaged import** (`unmanagedImportCollisions`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-unmanaged-import.ts:46-90`): already refuses every same-name clash, all types, 409.

Analysis re-read: an isolated reviewer at the contract-review tier re-verified every cited line and answered PASS WITH FIXES; all ten fixes are applied in this text.

Protocol statement: this card changes ADR-0048 §3.4's scope (every option but D) and, under C, ADR-0129's rule. No fleet protocol change.

## Premise (re-check commands)

The seat's audit (read-only, 2026-11-06, origin/main 802c98cf; re-verified by an isolated reviewer at 04f36b63) finds §3.4's premise false for most behaviour types: their runtime consumers resolve by bare name with no package context. Re-check:

```
grep -n "register(" packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts | head      # kernel 'metadata' service keyed (type, name); second register overwrites (~853-858); list dedups by name (~1407-1412)
sed -n 340,400p packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-precedence.ts   # one flow armed per name, ranked by package id alphabetically, warning logged
sed -n 4970,4990p packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts                   # action dispatch: by-name read with no package
sed -n 415,425p ../cloud/packages/service-ai/src/tools/action-tools.ts        # AI tool name action_<bare name>; second skipped (~1014-1017)
sed -n 250,260p ../cloud/packages/service-ai/src/tools/tool-registry.ts       # ToolRegistry.register overwrites silently
sed -n 100,110p packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts           # function registry keyed by bare name, last wins
sed -n 7900,7945p packages/objectql/src/registry.ts                           # managed install refuses only namespace / object / security-catalog / default-page clashes
```

Measured outcome per type (non-security types only):

| Runtime behaviour on a second same-name package item | Types |
|:--|:--|
| Both served correctly | job (a second holder is scheduled under `appId:jobName`, #21602), assignment rules (both evaluated) |
| One armed, warning logged, deterministic | flow |
| One served, **silently** | everything read through the kernel `metadata` service (agents, skills, external catalogs, api items via `listForIndex`), dispatch of an object-less action, AI tools (`action_<name>`, ToolRegistry), function handlers behind hooks, picklists, mappings, datasets/cubes, email templates, webhooks, two declared connectors |
| Package-scoped when the caller names the package, first match otherwise (reads only: a package-less save or delete of an ambiguous name already answers 409) | app, page, dashboard, report, standalone view, doc/book |

A security-relevant subset of the audit is with the maintainer separately and is not described here.

## The specific question

§3.4 promised coexistence; most execution-time consumers cannot honour it. Which contract replaces it?

## Options

| Option | What it does | What a customer sees | Workload |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A. One name, one holder, everywhere** | Extend the security catalog's refusal to every type whose consumers resolve without package context: install and package registration refuse a held name, naming both holders | The second app's install is refused with "rename X or uninstall Y"; nothing breaks silently, but two unrelated vendors' apps that both use `send_email` cannot coexist | `domain:engine` · 1–2 PRs · precedent #22197 (+1080/−103) and #22365 (+705/−43) for three types |
| **B-lite. Package-scope only the execution-time consumers** | Flow engine, object-less action dispatch, function registry and AI tool names resolve by (package, name); everything else stays as is | Fewer silent cases, but a cross-package trigger or action must still name a package, and every new consumer must remember to | several lanes (automation, runtime, ai) · ~4 PRs · no precedent |
| **B. Make every consumer package-aware** | Honour §3.4: each runtime consumer resolves by (package, name); cross-package references use the qualified `<packageId>:<name>` form | Same-name apps coexist; authors and AI must choose between a bare and a qualified reference at every cross-package site | many lanes (automation, runtime, ai, mcp, metadata, analytics, email, webhooks) · ~10+ PRs · no precedent |
| **C. Every name carries the namespace** | Extend ADR-0129's literal prefix to every package-authored top-level metadata name (`crm_send_email`), except names already derived from a prefixed object (fields, object extensions, container views) or already namespaced (translations `<ns>_<locale>`); enforced at `defineStack`/`os validate` and the save door; same-name clashes become impossible by construction | Names read `crm_send_email`; two apps never collide; one naming rule for everything | `domain:engine` + `domain:devx` · 3–4 PRs (rule + ADR amendment, load-time conversion or migration of first-party packages/templates/examples, lint) · no measured precedent for a cross-type naming rule; nearest landed: #22197 (+1080/−103) and #22365 (+705/−43), three types |
| **D. Status quo, fix consumers one by one** | Keep §3.4; file each silent consumer as found | Silent partial breakage continues until each is found | open-ended; no precedent |

Business meaning, one line each:
- A = "first come, first served" for names — like a shared drive that refuses a second file of the same name.
- B-lite = folders only for the files that run, links into them must still say which folder.
- B = every app gets its own folder, but every link must say which folder — the ADR-0028 shape.
- C = every app's files start with the app's code. Salesforce managed packages show every custom component as `ns__Name`; ServiceNow scoped apps prefix tables, fields, properties and script-include API names `x_<co>_<app>_` and scope the rest by application scope. Both derive the prefix; ObjectStack authors it literally (ADR-0129, for the one-writing-style reason).
- D = keep the bug, chase symptoms.

## Four axes (business stance)

- **① Long-term soundness.** C collapses two rules (objects prefixed; everything else bare, plus a growing per-type refusal list) into one, and matches how Salesforce names packaged components. A adds types to a refusal list, and that list grows with every new type. B and B-lite multiply package-qualified sites at consumers. D grows the bug surface.
- **② Real pull today.** The gallery installs several verified apps side by side and the maintainer has ruled that gallery apps prefix every name (2026-11-06); the marketplace ships multiple packages per environment. Measured incidents: #21602 (jobs, fixed), #28337 (dashboard overlay, fixed). No customer report of a flow or action clash yet.
- **③ AI errors.** C gives the AI one rule ("every name starts with your namespace"), and the error is loud at authoring. A is loud, but only at install, after the work is done. B and B-lite add a second spelling, the qualified form — the failure ADR-0129 exists to prevent — and a wrong guess resolves silently to another package. D is silent.
- **④ Startup non-sprawl.** A and C add no new key; C is a rule change plus a one-time migration. B and B-lite add a qualified-reference form to maintain forever.

## Recommendation

**C, phased.** End state, two years out: every package-authored name carries its namespace, as every custom component in a Salesforce managed package does; a collision cannot be authored by a namespaced package, and the per-type refusal list is a backstop only, not the contract.

Phasing (② and workload adjust the order only; the letter does not change):
1. **Now:** extend the existing registration refusal (A's mechanism) to the silent types. It closes silent mis-resolution for packages already in the field. After phase 3 it remains only as the backstop for the cases C cannot reach: packages that declare no namespace, the shared `base`/`system`/`sys` namespaces, and third-party packages inside the deprecation window.
2. **Next:** the existing `naming/namespace-prefix` lint rule (today intra-package duplicates only, its message calling the prefix optional) is re-widened to warn on every bare non-object name, and ADR-0048 §5's lint bullet is corrected in the same PR; scenario/gallery cards and first-party templates adopt the prefix (already ruled for the gallery; live card #30795).
3. **Then:** `defineStack`/`os validate` and the save door refuse a bare name in a package that declares a namespace, with the rename in the message; first-party packages migrate in the same release, and third-party packages get a load-time conversion or a deprecation window (the lane's design call).

Confidence gaps: the per-type list is an audit reading, not a booted two-package measurement; some names may be referenced by external callers (inbound webhook ids, connector ids), where a rename is a breaking change — phase 3 must list them. The migration size of first-party packages (hotcrm, templates, examples) is not measured.

Not chosen: A alone keeps two naming rules and a list that grows with each new type. B-lite leaves every new execution-time consumer to remember package scoping, and adds the qualified form. B is the ADR-0028 direction the maintainer rejected for AI-error reasons. D leaves silent breakage in place.

Self-check: on ① alone C; do ② ③ ④ flip it: no.

## Execution after the ruling

- C: the seat files three `domain:engine` / `domain:devx` cards (phase 1 refusal backstop; phase 2 lint + templates; phase 3 rule + ADR-0129 / ADR-0048 §3.4 amendment + migration), serial in that order, and records the ruling on objectstack-ai/cloud#3600.
- A: one `domain:engine` card (the phase-1 card alone) plus the ADR-0048 §3.4 narrowing.
- B or D: the seat files per-consumer cards from the table above.

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
os-decision-facets
- ① Long-term: C shrinks special cases (one naming rule, the refusal list a backstop only); A grows a list; B and B-lite multiply qualified-reference sites.
- ② Pull: gallery side-by-side installs (ruled 2026-11-06) and multi-package marketplace environments; incidents #21602, #28337 fixed; no flow/action report yet.
- ③ AI errors: C is one rule, loud at authoring; A loud at install; B and B-lite add a second spelling that fails silently; D silent.
- ④ Non-sprawl: A and C add no key; B and B-lite add a permanent qualified form.

Prior rulings read: "one name, one holder" → 10 hits (security catalog, #28337); "name collision" package metadata → 193 hits (relevant: #21602, #28337, #22307 A); "needs-user-decision prefix name" → #29594 (a different question); ADR-0048 §3.3–§3.5, §5, §6 + 2026-10-08 addendum, ADR-0129 D2–D4, ADR-0028 (Deferred), ADR-0146 D2/D8; thread: none
